CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 09.49:33.913 GT Tripped due to humming event caused by low gas pressure from the PRS.  Low gas pressure recorded at the PRS due to ESD system operation closing the inlet ESD valve XV4002 and pressure reduction skid valve XV4480.
Scada system alarms showed ESD system operated due to PRS common hand switch operated, (PRS\ESD\UA4002) and ESD trip from CDC control room (PRS\ESD\HS4002C) receipt of this alarm would indicate that the operator himself had activated the PRS trip by pushing the emergency trip button in the plant MCR This cannot of been the cause of the PRS trip due to the operator not pressing the push button in the MCR, this was witnessed by gas operations as they were present in the control room when the ESD system tripped. whilst the gas pressure supply to CDC did fall the cause of the unit trip was from combustion instability (humming). it is recognised  that the low gas pressure would have tripped the GT by activation of the low gas pressure trip signals however on this occasion 'Humming' occurred operating the MAX 3 protection trip before the low gas pressure trip signals were received. The load at the time of the trip was 414MWgen (full load in 'OTC operation).
TITLE: GT Trip from PRS ESV’s closing

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

SAP notification 21495373 refers. 

As a result of the leak, instrument cables supplying the LP circ pump differential pressure transmitters have been damaged causing the pumps to trip.  A SIM has been raised to prevent the pumps from tripping and a unit run back occurring. SIM 21495433 refers.
TITLE: Unit 4 South East 19m level HRSG casing split, exhaust gasses at extreme temperatures escaping into the HRSG building.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

Also The ROMS informed to look into logic/ events leading to unit trip also.
TITLE: low frequency alarm followed by Unit trip

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 13.20 on Friday 18th February 2022 the integrity of Unit 7 Chimney Stack failed in high winds. The chimney stack collapsed and folded at a height of approx. 35-40m onto the corner of the HRSG roof, causing the top of the stack to collapse down the north side of the building in between Unit 7 and Unit 6.
Unit 7 GT Trip Push Button was initiated from the CCR at 13.21.
Unit was shut down as safely as possible with the GT & ST going On Barring. U61 was also shutdown in a controlled manner as a precaution, whilst U81 was already non operational due to Outage activities progressing.
A full site evacuation was ordered, with all site personnel and contractor workers being fully accounted for. There were no reported injuries or off site local impacts as a result of the collapse.

This incident occurred during storm Eunice, with a red weather warning Met Office alert having been issued earlier that day (having already been upgraded from an Amber alert issued the previous evening). Site had already implemented the high winds procedure which restricted any external work activities. This measure was agreed and communicated following the morning meeting performance dialogue. At approx. 12:00 hrs, as a further control measure all non essential works were ceased on site, with all contractor workers being stood down and returning to their respective office/messroom facilities.
TITLE: U7 Chimney Stack integrity failure (external RCA in progress - (EXTENDED 31/12/2022 Panel of Enquiry) 14/10

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

CASE_DESCRIPTION: On run up this morning the steam turbine tripped at 44Hz due to low reheat steam temperature. Steam turbine had to slowed using the E shaft vac valve. This is infact the steam turbine program looking for X5 which is lost, the Start up device appears to be a red herring. We found that even if the steam turbine is selected to fast from a trip it still looks for X5 positive which is not the same criteria of a HOF start. Hence the start up device is not the issue. Defects have been entered for the reheat thermocouples reading low.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
U1 Boiler Recirc pump tripped/came out of service on Sat 07/03 @ 08:20 hrs with no abnormal alarms received, we were unable to restart the pump because when the pump was found out of service on a panel check, we were just outside of the 2.5hr window where we allowed restart it.
We have done some preliminary investigations and it appears the pump shut down around the time we were carrying out our routine weekend checks.
The particular checks in question involve us pressing the A & B side drum hydrastep level check alarm test buttons that are located on the Unit ESD panel, to confirm the alarm works.
We have carried out a controlled test and it appears that if both A & B side hydrasteps level buttons are tested at the same time, or in quick succession (both alarms up at the same time) this then takes the pump out of service on a drum low level (drum level low should trip the pump under normal conditions), however if the hydrasteps are tested one at a time then the pump remains in service. No alarms are received to indicate the recirc pump has tripped.
TITLE: Operational loss (not process safety) - U1 Boiler recirc pump tripped / came out of service

CASE_DESCRIPTION: On 1st August 2020 CO2 in the fire suppression tank warmed and increased in pressure sufficiently to lift the pressure safety valve at 25 Bar and -12OC. On investigation the cooling compressor and fan were found not running. Various electrical and mechanical checks were performed to identify the reason for the non-running cooling system, finally a reset button on the compressor control pressure switch rectified the fault and the CO2 began to cool again. At 16:00 on the same day a subsequent check found that although the pressure and temperature had dropped to -15OC and 22 Bar, ice formed under the safety valve seat during its lifting had caused the valve to not correctly seat and loose further CO2 to a mass of 7.2 tonnes. The minimum mass required to protect the unit during operation is 8.0 tonnes so the unit was broken down until a delivery could be arranged.
TITLE: U4 Fire Suppression CO2 Tank low level

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During a routine water treatment plant stream regeneration it was found that acid had leaked from the system into the acid bund. The process was immediately stopped, and isolation valves closed. The acid within the bund was fuming off at this point making it difficult to approach the area, but estimations of level was about 3-4mm. Personnel withdraw from the area and opened exterior doors to provide some ventilation.
Email sent to all members of staff advising of the situation and asking them to cascade this to their direct reports and contractors.
After some discussion on the way forward and a Dynamic risk assessment had been carried out, an Operation Technician donned suitable PPE and respirator and re-entered the WTP room and pumped out the bund into the main sump. The bund was then washed down and pumped into the main sump, ready to be sent to the neutralisation tank.
The cause of the leak is suspected to be vent from the double block and bleed valve. There was no evidence of wet on the motor support plate or surrounding pipework.
TITLE: Acid leak in acid bund

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

Upon immediate investigation it was found that the flow to the cell of the instrument had been interrupted by "slime" but the constant head device was still flowing so there wasn't and alarm indicting loss of flow. 
On the night shift 11/09/19 when dosing again the same situation occurred and again dosing was stopped as soon as the alarm
initiated and the purge flow adjusted accordingly. 
The C & I team investigated as soon as they arrived on the following day shift to confirm that the cell had blocked again. Although this was not a breach of our permit there are still implications and reporting required.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the 24/10 U3 was fired and steam to set occurred, it was showing high extraction pump conductivities >5uS before and after column. on the return to service unit 3 boiler chemistry deviated from target conditions. The extraction pump chemistry went into alarm state 3 (>1.0uS after column conductivity) during its on load run and the boiler water chemistry followed with the after column conductivity peaking at 51uS (alarm state 3). 
Due to the unit being ran to increase pressure for trevi testing there was no caustic dosing in the boiler water therefore no
boiler water protection. The pH of the feed flow and boiler water remained beneath the required level for the duration. LP dosing only occurred whilst the unit was generating. 
The boiler was dosed on the morning of 26/10 with a firing dose after discussions with a boiler team representative and the trevi continued after the dose had been added. The boiler was fired for 3hours after the trevi test was completed to facilitate blowdown and dosing of the boiler water. There was no steam sample available to assess the amount of sodium that has passed through the attemperator sprays into the superheaters. Both shells of the condenser had saw dust added to try and slow the ingress of contaminants and it was questioned if a condenser shell could be taken out of service to help to identify which shell the leak was in.
TITLE: Operational loss - U3 high extraction pump conductivities

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
CDC module was at full load.
A large flame was witnessed on the control room CCTV coming from the west side of the top of the gas turbine.
A decision was made to manually trip the gas turbine from the control room  back panel emergency stop push button as simultaneously the fire alarm panel began to sound.
The above all proceeded within approximately 30 seconds of the flames being witnessed.
The site evacuation alarm was sounded along with a tannoy instruction to evacuate site.
The station MEL was redec'd to 0MW and remitted with energy trading.
The plant was observed as it was shutdown and the visible flames stopped on the tripping of the plant.  
The main gas valve 10EKG70AA001 was closed and gas vented to remove all gas from the building. The FGPH outlet valves were manually closed to 10EFG70AA001 passing.
Approximately 15 minutes after the GT being tripped a visual inspection was made of the GT which confirmed the dislodging of a flange thought to be that of the flame eye and lagging being emitted from the blow off pipework on the west side of the GT.
As there was no further risk to personnel the site evacuation was ended with the UMC remaining off limits and locked down.
Further inspection and repair planning commenced with the Engineering Team.
TITLE: Gas Turbine Combustion Chamber Flame Eye Failure.

CASE_DESCRIPTION: A recent Gas detection panel fault had closed the sites main Gas valve 10EKG70AA001 on protection. During the unit start up 3 attempts were made to start the GT for it’s DP run scheduled for 15:00 – 21:00. Each attempt failed due to time out of the fuel gas program as a result of 10EKG70AA001 not opening in time. On the 3rd start attempt, the valve was locally observed to see what was happening. It became apparent that the valve was trying to run open but not moving more than a fraction. Numerous attempts were made to drive the valve open, both electrically from the DCS, locally and manually using the handwheel. It was concluded the valve was either mechanically jammed or pressure locked. After some discussion, the decision was made to try and reduce the pressure upstream of the valve by venting off gas from the pre-heater. This was successful and allowed the valve to be re-opened.
TITLE: Main Gas Valve would not open.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On May 14th at 21:45 hrs, Both CPUs were running from T-302 (crude mix: Doba 96.88%, Dar 1.21%, Nile 1.91%) and panel operator found feed pump discharge and column pressure increasing beyond control, both units forced to shut down suspecting water shot.

During above the operations team noticed increased levels on back pressure in the Flash column, which could lead to an activation of  automatic trip sequence shutting down the crude feed pumps (P-1-001 & P-2-001), all other main equipment will follow to shut down after trip sequence. Due to this and to avoid further process and plant safety and potential H&S problems both units taken to  shut down. There was a loss of production of 6 hours 45 minutes in CPU 1 and 7 hours 35 minutes in CPU 2. 


The CPUs are prepared as per design to take up to 3% suspended water but not to process free water, this is perceived as the main risk for this type of events. Similar events had occurred on 3rd March 2021. One of them was automatic trip due higher P in the Flash column. 

The most likely scenario in case of not addressing this situation in time is would be a pop up of the Pressure Safety Valve (PSV) in the Flask Column. In this case the affected unit will suffer unplanned unavailability for the reinstallation of the PSV. In case of additional failure of the PSV, the failure could lead to a malfunction in the Flash column potentially leading to release of vapours (depending on where within the flask columns the failure materializes it might lead to release of vapours, crude etc).
TITLE: Water shot incident

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On 4th March 2021, 23:30 hrs the VTTI operations team observed black smoke from the stack of CPU-1 furnace (tag no. ME-1-001) (see Annex 1 “Annex 1_CPU-1 Furnace stack smoke email VTTI_20210304.pdf”). As the thick smoke was continuously coming out the operators stopped the furnace at 23:45 hrs and the unit was taken into long circulation. At 02:30 hours on 5th March 2021 the CPU-1 was put under short circulation (see Annex 2 “Annex 2_CPU Log Sheet as of 4th March 2021”).
The following day, the furnace control system (BMS) was restarted by Uniper E&I Maintenance team for a default reset of error values. After this CPU-1 furnace was re-started 2 times on a trial basis, checking that continuous white smoke was coming from the stack. Subsequently firing of ME-1-001 was stopped waiting for further investigation, with the final objective of finding the root cause of the incident. For the investigation it was decided to get support from specialized 3rd parties such as Harris Pye (HP) and Bureau Veritas(BV).
In total because of this incident CPU-1 was down ca. 30 days from March 4th, 2021 23:30 hrs until April 3rd 14:00 hrs.
TITLE: Thick black smoke from CPU-1 Furnace stack

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On March 3rd 05:45 hrs, right after the feed tank change over from T-303 (crude mix: Doba 40.69%, Dar 34.35%, Nile 24.95%) to T-301 (crude mix: Nile 22.28%, Doba 73.50%, Dar 4.24%) both units had to be shut down due to a water shot.  
 
Following the tank feed switching operation the operations team noticed increased levels on back pressure in the Flash column, which could lead to an activation of  automatic trip sequence shutting down the crude feed pump (P-001), all other main equipment will follow to shut down after trip sequence. Due to this and to avoid further process and plant safety and potential H&S problems both units taken to  shut down. There was no loss of production as it happened during start up process. 
 

The CPUs are prepared as per design to take up to 3% suspended water but not to process free water, this is perceived as the main risk for this type of events. Similar events had occurred only 3 times in the asset lifetime, including this one. One of them was automatic trip due higher P in the Flash column. 

The most likely scenario in case of not addressing this situation in time is would be a pop up of the Pressure Safety Valve (PSV) in the Flask Column. In this case the affected unit will suffer unplanned unavailability for the reinstallation of the PSV. In case of additional failure of the PSV, the failure could lead to a malfunction in the Flash column potentially leading to release of vapours (depending on where within the flask columns the failure materializes it might lead to release of vapours, crude etc).  

The crude feed tank that was being used , T-301,  had been last operated by Uniper Ops team, on February 24th, due to vessel discharge operations was. In this case the available time for tank preparation was sufficient.
TITLE: Water shot incident

CASE_DESCRIPTION: On 16th February ’20 at early morning around 0300 hrs. the Field operator during his rounds at CPU-1 noticed fumes and HFO leaking through the insulation cladding of the suction loop from Pump-1-007 (Flash column HFO R/D pump) suction side. Field operator immediately informed at the CCR and the pump was stopped immediately, and the plant taken to ESD, pump isolated & depressurized. DNO tag was provided for suction and discharge block valves. The area was cordoned off. The HFO leakage was about 50 liters but that was onto the pump skid tray, and the leak didn’t splash or spread out elsewhere. There was no personnel hurt, no contamination, as it was contained and no property damage as well. Initial findings on opening up the insulation cladding; On the 2‘‘ branch piping where Chemical SR1394 was being injected on a trial basis there was pin hole discovered, which was the source of the leak, and later after the system was cooled, drained out completely and inerted, the spool piece was removed and found that there was heavy corrosion on the internal base of the spool. Suspecting the pitted hole due to excessive corrosion contributed by the chemical being injected. Prior to start of use, it was confirmed and verified by the vendor that it was compatible with MS, CS & SS, but in reality it seemed that chemical was not compatible with CS at all, and had severe effects on CS.
TITLE: CPU-1 P-1-007 Suction piping chemical injection leak

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At approximately 13.29 the G as panel in control room failed initiating a GT protection level 1 & 2 trip.
It was assumed that voltage fluctuations from the SFC had possibly caused a supply MCB to the panel to trip. (Running the SFC has been known to play havoc with some actuators on site, in particular ones associated with the aux boiler). Initial investigations revealed the power source for the gas panel (415v switchboard 10GMA06) had not tripped but further investigation within the gas panel were made which ascertained there was no 240v power to it’s internal power supply. A small fast blow anti surge fuse was found blown in the 240v supply line to the power supply unit. A new one was sourced and fitted. 240v power was now restored to the power supply unit, but there was no 27v DC output from the unit. Although the DC supply healthy light was lit on the front of the panel (from the back up batteries), there was no functionality from the gas panel at all.
Members of the Engineering team were called to site and the power supply unit was removed and dismantled to reveal it was badly burnt out inside. An alternative 24v DC power supply unit was obtained and temporarily installed which allowed the gas panel to be reinstated.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Gas turbine overspeeds, steam turbine overspeeds & steam turbine HP stop valve/governor valve tested successfully. Plant was stable and running at 400MW.
12:09hrs TST IP SV + CV Left FAIL 18MAB11EA121. Whereby, IP steam turbine governor valve closed fully, but the IP stop valve remained in intermediate mode (18MAB11AA001). Result was worsened vacuum >250mbar causing the steam turbine to trip (18MAX43EZ903_XU51). REMIT call submitted to Trading approximately 12:10hrs. Load dropped to SEL, drum levels controlled, air cooled condenser demin sprays put into service and sequencer selected to bypass. Grid were called to inform them of the situation.
By 12:17hrs, SEL was achieved. Due to standby to bypass being selected, gas turbine continued to deload.
At about 12:28hrs, Trading called requesting a REMIT update: 70MW from 12:30hrs to 13:30hrs. Then, between 13:30 and 13:43hrs increase load from 70 to 240MW. Remain at SEL until 15:00hrs.
Grid called and updated.
~ 13:34hrs programme device became disabled on the steam turbine and was manually given an ON command. Steam turbine became to ramp up from 70 to 240MW.
Steam turbine, at the time of writing is stable, and control valve stresses are improving (26 & 68% for HP and IP valves respectively.)

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

Multiple notifications under 21347109 are available to view valve fault history.  
During the valve fault the flow rate on the heating water side dropped and shut down the fuel gas preheater program.
 When the fuel gas preheater shuts down cooler natural gas flows to the GT burners. During this transition from Hot Gas to cooler gas the Gas turbine suffers combustion instability and combustion chamber rumble occurs causing GT Humming protection systems to operate.  
On the morning of 29-03-2021 the GT Humming protection operated as a direct result of cooler natural gas temperatures causing 0.2s to be added to the humming counter, there was a slight drop in load as the GT setpoint controller was switched off causing a slight imbalance during a load transient.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
IP casing diff (10MAB50FT051) was noted to be higher than normal. Seal steam valves checked out on plant (previous cause of such a high casing diff) both being in the correct position. Unable to run Unit co-ordination early due to 60min notice BOAI.
Unit coordination ran straight away to try and minimise delay. GT loaded up to 145mW and sat there until casing diff cleared some 30 minutes later releasing the Steam Turbine. The 30 minutes delay caused an imbalance of 150mW/h.
TITLE: Operational Loss due Steam Turbine IP casing diff >30degC.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the operator's routine walk around at 8:00 PM, hydrocarbon fumes observed from CPU 1 HE-1-002 channel head top, through a small opening. CCR was notified immediately. The CCR operator initiated ERP and called for ERT members. The furnace and plant were stopped by a CCR DCS operator. 
Other Operator from CPU 2 also arrived at the site. The flame was extinguished with DCP fire extinguishers immediately and the steam was provided through the steam hose. The incident commander and members of ERT arrived on the scene and followed FERP. The channel head area was cooled with water through a fire hose reel.
The deluge system was not activated and also no fire alarm was activated as the flame was extinguished and under control immediately.
No continuous leak was detected and no leakage to the ground was found.
The plant was cooled down and flushed with diesel in order to remove the insulation and inspect the heat exchanger.
TITLE: HE-1-002 flange leak, fumes and minor flame.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 16:40h the unit had a full load trip from 386MW/SO. ROMS was called at 16:51h. The unit was REMIT'ed out to 21:30h at 0MW. after investigation it was found that the trip was caused by aIP By-pass trip signal (10MAN51EZ001) which was instigated by a IP water injection flow protection (10MAN53EZ110). The IP by-pass spray water flow went below 0Kgs (-0.5kgs) on channels A and B, which has caused the unit trip. The IP by-pass was closed at the time and the IP Throttle valve was at 99% open. Paul Cockram and Will Hammond investigated the trip. A temporary simulation has been put in place whilst a Siemens recommend MOD is put in place.

Unit re-synchronised at 20:42 .
TITLE: CDC Full Load Trip

CASE_DESCRIPTION: A program of structural work was in progress across the 4 GT air intakes. Whilst  continuing the work within GT 12 air intake top section, a member of the working party noticed smoke escaping from the bottom section of the filter house. No hot work at that time was been carried out in the bottom section. Work was immediately stopped and an attempt was made by the working party to extinguish using fire extinguishers  at the point of work. This was unsuccessful and the control room was contacted, and the site alarm was raised at 15:33 evacuating the site. The site team was dispatched and fought the fire using fire hoses from ground level. The 1st fire tender arrived on site at 15:46 and continued to fight the fire. The fire was declared out at 16:04. Hot work as currently been stopped on site. A full investigation is ongoing
TITLE: Fire in GT 12 air intake filter house

CASE_DESCRIPTION: Unit was on outage, with the open cycle CW pump in service,  at 11:48 control room operator heard a bang through the open window, and alarm  - Pres Beh open cy pum < 1.5 bar received.  Pump discharge pressure had been running at 2.9 bar but took a spike down to 0.5 bar, pump remained in service. ST forced cooling in progress, condenser vacuum and hotwell level remained constant. Outside operator observed water emanating from the ground and into the rain water pit and coming up through the drainage sump covers.  At the time is wasn't clear how fast water levels would rise and how much water there would be so the final discharge drainage pumps were left in service for 30 minutes until levels receded, before manually tripping.  water level has now soaked back into the ground but has left a sink hole by the drainage pumps
TITLE: Main Cooling Water - Pipe failure - Loss of containment

CASE_DESCRIPTION: Unit was coming back from outage and the GFR control  oil system was put in service.  Oil was found coming out of HP lower governor filter diff pressure switch.  Technician managed to shut away the pressure switch to stop the leak.  The pressure switch was replaced during the outage.  Upon closer inspection it was found that the rating on the side of the pressure switch was 12 bar or less.  The system it was fitted on runs at 120 bar.  The markings on the side of the pressure switch were very small and almost ineligible. After investigation it was found this indication was sensing pressure range and not max pressure. Switch was rated for system integrity wise.
TITLE: Pressure switch failure leading to oil release

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Recently at Ratcliffe we've taken delivery of 600 new HID access control cards.  As of last month our previously issued E.On access control cards ran out and we started issuing from the new batch.

After a few days a couple of users informed us that when setting up SecurePrint on their new cards, when scanning in on the printers instead of taking them through the registration process it logged them in as another user.

We believe that this is due to the stored numbers on the two active people's different cards being the same, and/or SecurePrint not using the site code portion of the access control cards.

This is a data protection risk as there is a chance that these users with duplicate card numbers could print sensitieve personal data off the SecurePrint queue from that account that they are incorrectly logged into.

I've attached a flow diagram to explain the problem.

Fundamentally we believe that the fragmented way that Access Control cards are issued across the company and having a company wide access control card swipe system for the printers is why the risk of duplicate numbers on Access control cards is a data protection risk.

There is also a potential that these duplicate cards could allow someone access to another site that they are not authorised, but we don't believe this risk is high as the access control systems should use the site codes as well, but this will need investigating.
TITLE: Potential for Duplicate Swipe Card Numbers to be allocated with different Access Control Cards

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Unit BOAI’d to service, there was no PN for the entire period….

Unit tripped shortly after start-up on 30th due to low HP feed flow. Feed reg bypass valve faulted. Fault rectified but not in time to save unit from protection trip.

Mel Redeclared to 0MWso @ 12:50hrs 
MEL Redeclared available (sloping MEL to reflect run up) from 14:00hrs 

HP Feed Reg Bypass valve faulted causing HP Feed low flow protection, operator managed to regain flow and re-set GT emergency shutdown, the situation repeated itself and the operator was unable to re-set the GT protection shutdown before unit de-synchronised. 

A GT Protection Shutdown is NOT a GT trip it’s a forced failsafe shutdown following a de-load ramp rate therefore no GT trip penalty and no purge required.
TITLE: HP FEED REG BYPASS FAULT

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

It was then discovered that the breaker was still in local operation mode. The breaker was placed back into remote operation and the 415v boards normalised.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During a run up to FSNL. 
21:22 Bearing 2 vib > max 1 alarm. DCS showed 20mm/s but this is the max of its range. GE suggested the GT should have tripped automatically but it didn't. 
21:23 GT reached FSNL and vibration has dropped

The reason for the GT not tripping on high vibration was investigated. The Bentley Nevada set points were checked and the trip levels are set at 14.7 when the GT trip matrix says they should be 11.8. With the 1.5x mulitplier on start up the 14.7 became 22.05 which was above the range of the instrument (20mm/s) so the GT did not trip. Once at FSNL the multipliers are not in effect so the trip limit was back to 14.7. 

Further investigation required.
TITLE: GT vibration trip setting

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There have been multiple cases of low level hydrogen leaks detected on both SC10 and SC20 synchronous condensers during offline periods.

July 7th 2022

The synchronous condenser was shutdown due to the need for a Mod 2 400KV grid isolation for maintenance activities.

Whilst the SC20 Generator was at standstill a hydrogen leak alarm was received on the gas detector panel CYE01 in the Killingholme control room. Investigations at that time could not detect a genuine leak although the reading appeared to last for approximately 30 seconds and peaked at 20% LEL. This alarm was detected at both ends of the Generator on both HD005 and HD006. 

Later as the Hydrogen Purity Concentration procedure was being carried out these alarms were received again. This time a noticeable leak could be heard within the turbine hall also. These readings peaked at 40% LEL and the detection lasted for several minutes. 

To clarify the first alarm was received with the shaft at standstill and no work being carried out and the second alarm was received when the shaft was still at standstill but hydrogen filling was taking place.

A further leak alarm was detected when  SC20 was put on barring up to 200RPM using the oil system

Aug 21st 2022

Again a 400KV outage was required for maintenance activities on MOD1.

Again, Killingholme OPS took the opportunity to attempt to sweeten the generator hydrogen purity. There were similar leaks of hydrogen detected as there was on SC20 above but in slightly different.

* Whilst at standstill during the H2 sweetening process

* Whilst at standstill following completion of the sweetening process.

* Whilst on barring on the return to operation

19/12/2022

Leak alarms were once again raised when SC20 was stopped to carry out repairs on GT21 GCB.  Leaks stopped once the unit was put back on barring.
TITLE: SC10/20 Generator Hydrogen Leak alarms.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
From Enerlytics alert dated 22/03/2023 @ 14:38
During routine OLVMS monitoring, UTG noticed higher than normal levels of vibration along the ST shaft line during the run up on 16th March. The highest levels were seen on the IP/LP Eccentricities where levels peaked at 290 um pk-pk with the unit at 842 rpm, during a normal run up a typical amplitude at this speed would be 25-50 um pk-pk. The change in vibration was 1/rev driven suggesting the unit had run up with a temporary bend.

A review of the barring file prior to this run up shows that the turbine remained stationary for approximately 1 hour following the previous run down on the evening of 15th March. The barring file shows the rotor straightening across the barring period, however the elevated vibration levels had not fully subsided before the start of the run up. If the unit was had remained on barring for a few more hours the rotor may had been able to fully straighten prior to starting.

Once the machine reached full speed and was loaded up, the vibration levels subsided as the machine straighten. Subsequent run ups and run downs have passed by without incident, comparing well to previous and giving no cause for concern.
TITLE: Unit 6 Steam Turbine High Vibrations on Run-Up.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Contacted by NRW via phone with confirmation by email regarding complaint:

As discussed, at 13:30 on Friday 28th February NRW received an incident report from a member of public.

It states the following

Caller concerned about clouds of smoke/gas discharging from Connahs Quay power station noticed yesterday and is happening again today. Caller has tried contacting site direct, but the number given is not being answered. Caller says she doesn't want an excuse of "condensation", as she claims "condensation would evaporate, but these clouds are hanging about for 2 days".

Reply to NRW from Environmental Advisor:

Hello and many thanks for your email. 

We’re keen to ensure all environmental complaints / enquiries regarding the Power station are answered as quickly as possible. As you may be aware, last weekend (Feb 28th to March 2nd) has been a time of very low wind levels, bright sunshine, clear skies and generally cold atmospheric conditions. 

Shown below is a screen grab of the weather entry for Hawarden weather station for Feb 28th 2025

As a result we were called to run three CCGT Units for the majority of Friday and at times four units ran together over the weekend. 

I’ve checked with our operational staff and can state we were called to run three CCGT Units for the majority of Friday and at times four units ran together over the weekend,  on all these occasions the machines ran successfully, with no incident or issue and well within our emission monitoring limits as specified by the site’s Natural Resources Wales regulated Environmental Permit. As you may recall our Gas Treatment Plant closed in 2023 and is no longer operational. 

As a result, I can only conclude that the complainant is referring to the significant cooling tower plume which would be produced by active generational levels on a cold and crisp winter day. The uncommon environmental conditions are very likely to result in the large scale formation of such plume, made more visible by the cold clear winter skies. 

This emission of cooling tower vapour is permissible inline with current environmental legislation. Should you have the ability to contact the complainant then we would be interested to know which phone number was rung and failed to contact the power station. Clearly we’re keen to ensure there is always a clean means of communication in times of potential incident complaint and we can seek to correct any incorrect phone numbers which might exist anywhere. 

Please don’t hesitate to contact myself should you require any further information regarding this issue.
TITLE: NRW received an incident report from a member of public

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A near hit incident occurred involving a forklift and a stack of heavy steel plates. The incident took place at outside Unit 1 turbine hall at approximately 14:05

Details of the Incident:

Forklift Operator:  PES 
Equipment Involved, Steel Plates

Sequence of Events:
The forklift was transporting a stack of heavy steel plates.
As the forklift took a corner, the plates began to slide off the forks.
The sliding plates posed a significant risk of falling and potentially causing injury or damage.

Immediate Actions Taken:
The forklift operator immediately stopped the vehicle to prevent further movement of the plates.
The area was cordoned off to ensure safety until the situation was stabilized.
Additional personnel were called to assist in safely repositioning the plates.

Root Cause Analysis:
Load Securing: It was identified that the steel plates were not adequately secured before transport.
Forklift Speed: The speed at which the corner was taken may have contributed to the instability of the load.
Corner Handling: The angle and method of turning the corner were reviewed for safety compliance.
TITLE: U1 OUTAGE - FLT Transporting Generator Casing Steel Plate

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Sequence of event on April 21st 
1.	23:35hrs CPU-1&2 taken on long circulation.
2.	01:45hrs Feed tank changed over from T-302 to T-303.
3.	Non urgent alarm received in SCADA, related to CPU-1 Furnace. Firing did not stop
4.	Operators checked in Furnace BMS PLC and found Naphtha KOD (knock Out Drum) Level low low alarm. Level indication found 0. 
5.	Furnace stopped from SCADA immediately at 02:07hrs.

Found LCV-1712 is open. On checking in field found KOD level is very High. Drained more than 10 buckets of Naphtha and level brought down less than the low pressure impulse line of the Level Transmitter. Level Transmitter low pressure impulse line drained and indication restored in PLC. Alarm reset done in PLC and furnace started at 03:45 hrs. 

The suspected root cause is a momentary malfunction of LCV-1712 or LT-1711 the reason for this is under analysis. LCV-1712 - Level control valve maintain a constant level of NAPHTHA supply to KOD. LT-1711 controls the level of Naphtha in KOD and sends signal to LCV-1712 to open/ close the LCV-1712 valve for supply of Nphtha based on set values.
TITLE: KOD tank

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the committed work program for Friday (1st March), there was a request to isolate both the Anion & Cation on Stream 1.  Stream 1 has not been in service for many years and the request was to unbox the vessels and pump out the resin in preparation for decommissioning the stream.  Stream 1 has sat isolated for at least 10 years.  Overnight the keys were retrieved from the CPO's key safe and all the isolation points were checked, and the old E-on caution labels were replaced with Uniper labels.  As the vessels had been isolated for so long, and there is no external indication of level, it was an unknown as to the level within the vessels.  The Anion and Cation drains to the effluent sump were opened, and a flow was heard immediately.  Also the tell tale drains and vents to atmosphere were opened.  I would estimate that the vessels were at least half full prior to starting draining.  As the vessels were draining there was a pungent smell noted,  we remained in the WTP as the vessels drained and continued to apply further isolations to the acid & caustic dilution tanks in preparation for future de-commissioning.  The smell appeared to us to dissipate fairly quickly, so once the vessels were fully drained, the drain valves were locked shut to complete the isolation.  We returned to the Permit office to prepare the PFW.  When passing through the control room there was several comments made about a foul strong smell, and it was quickly realised it was emanating from our skin, overalls and clothing.  I returned to the WTP to assess the odour, and on re-entering the WTP the smell was extremely strong.  But again within a few minutes I became accustomed to the smell. 

Due to the pungency of the odour, I stated (in the further precautions on the PFW) that a selected person should attend the unboxing of the vessels and carry out an atmosphere check prior to starting work.

I understand that prior to the unboxing, discussions between the selected person and duty control person resulted in the PFW being withdrawn until the source of the smell could be identified, and to ascertain if it was in anyway harmful to health.  I was asked to input a Synergy tonight (2nd March).

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When taking U6 off load the HP bypass spray wasn't controlling properly causing high after bypass temperatures and tripping the HP Bypass.This is a known issue so we were expecting this to happen. Due to the Bypass trip the HP header pressure rises as the steam has nowhere to go. When the bypass was reset it was noticed that the process value on the HP bypass was struggling to meet the set point and was lagging behind quite a bit. This caused the HP header to rise significantly and the safety valves lifted. At this point the unit was off load but it was noticed that the GT EV burners were still lit adding to the high steam pressure situation. We tried to put an 'OFF' on the GT sequencer but this didn't work so we used the emergency trip button located on the unit desk. Once the flames were out the pressure started to subside but the HP bypass was still clearly not controlling as it should.Due to the significance off the HP bypass the unit was MEL'd to 0MW until 12:00 01/10/24
There are x3 issues here:
1. HP Bypass spray water control not controlling well enough to stop the HP Bypass tripping on high temperatures
2. Hp Bypass process value not following the set point as it should.
3. The GT not shutting down correctly and taking the flames out when the Circuit breaker was opened.
TITLE: U6 HP Bypass failed to operate correctly and boiler safety valves operated

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On unit 3 run-up A1 Re-heater Intercept valve tripped and went undetected. The unit was synchronised and proceeded to load up, at approx. 440MW Hot Re-heater safety valve 166 lifted as a result of the intercept valve being tripped. Although the HP exhaust pressure was only 40 bar, indicating the safety valve had lifted “light” (there are also 4 other R/htr safety valves passing on this unit).
The unit load was reduced to 230MW initially thus reducing R/htr pressure and enable a gag to be installed, unsuccessful the load had to be reduced further to 20MW allowing successful fitting of the gag. Unit load was then returned back to full capacity. 
The problem of the tripping intercept valves on fast (5 minute) run-ups has been highlighted several times in the past and a previous OIT raised. Also, the turbine valve tripping isn’t highlighted significantly enough, meaning operators can miss this crucial problem.
TITLE: PSNH  - U3 re-heater Intercept valve tripping leading to r/htr safety valve 166 to lift.

The fuse carrier to be used was identified (the fuse holder+fuse was missing so the SAP didnt have to remove it). The plan was to connect into the outgoing side of the fuse carrier so the SAP physically covered the live side of the fuse carrier with a caution card and protected the area with caution tape. 
When the document was cancelled the CP informed the SAP that what was thought to be the outgoing side was in actual fact the live side which he discovered when he tested for dead. At this point instead of returning to the SAP the CP removed the isolation and connected into the true outgoing side of the fuse carrier and completed the job.
TITLE:
Point of isolation interfered without consultation with SAP.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
